name: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Ltd
title: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Ltd - 532296 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Glenmark Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23.1% YoY to INR40,185 million; base business growth was above 18% excluding ISB 2001 deferred income.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations was INR40,185 million, up 23.1% YoY from INR32,644 million, with North America (+41.1%, or +19.8% core excluding ISB 2001 deferred out-licensing income) and emerging markets (+27.7%) the main drivers. India formulations grew 15.5% to INR14,321 million, outgrowing IPM by about 6 points in Q1 per IQVIA. Europe was muted at +11.9% as management shifts the mix toward branded respiratory and dermatology products. Management said gross margin was held despite higher API, packing and logistics costs linked to the geopolitical situation, and reiterated a 21-22% full-year margin guide.

financial_highlights.metric: Base business growth excluding ISB 2001 deferred income

financial_highlights.change: +41.1% YoY; +19.8% core excluding ISB 2001 deferred income
Guided at 7-8% of revenue going forward; management said Q1 was a bit lower
Management said cash only; gross debt zero maintained

segments.name: India formulations
segments.commentary: INR14,321 million, +15.5% YoY; +18.1% in Q1 and +14.3% MAT June per IQVIA vs IPM at 12.2% and 10%. Ranked 13th with 2.37% share; 11 brands in IPM top 300.

segments.name: India Consumer Care (GCC)
segments.commentary: Primary sales INR1,558 million, +28% YoY. Candid grew over 30% across variants; LA SHIELD mid-single digit; Scalpe and Bontress grew very strongly.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: INR10,974 million, +41.1% YoY; +19.8% core excluding ISB 2001 deferred income. Nine products launched in the quarter; RYALTRIS US commercialisation started; fluticasone 44 mcg first ANDA approval with 180-day CGT exclusivity.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: INR7,472 million, +11.9% YoY. Branded portfolio grew well; RYALTRIS gaining share via Menarini; WINLEVI launched in UK, Nordics, CEE, Spain and Portugal. Management guides high single-digit FY27 growth and double-digit from FY28.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: INR7,304 million, +27.7% YoY. Russia secondary sales grew 12-plus% (IQVIA MAT May 2026); APAC double-digit secondary growth; RYALTRIS launch in Brazil planned for H2 FY27.

segments.name: RYALTRIS (global)
segments.commentary: Marketing applications in more than 90 countries; commercialised in 57 markets with 10 more expected over coming quarters; global secondary sales growth upwards of 40% YoY.

segments.name: IGI pipeline
segments.commentary: ISB 2001 (ABBV-2001): more than 160 subjects dosed in TRIgnite Phase I. ISB 2301 IND planned later in FY27; INR70 million quarterly spend allocated to IGI.

guidance_outlook: Full-year EBITDA/operating margin guide of 21-22% reiterated; management expects growth in the US and India to offset war-related cost pressure.
India business growth guided at 12-15% on a consistent basis going forward.
Europe: high single-digit growth for FY27, returning to double-digit from FY28 as branded launches scale.
Net working capital kept within 115 days for the full year (currently well below); gross debt to remain zero.
Aumolertinib India/EM first commercial launch expected in H2 FY27; QiNHAYO (envafolimab) first launch in FY28; Trastuzumab Rezetecan MA filings begin Q2 FY27.
Two to three additional US respiratory launches (110 mcg MDI, nasal spray Rx, ipratropium) expected in H2 FY27; fluticasone 44 full-quarter benefit expected in Q2.
Management expects geopolitical cost pressures to persist for at least two more quarters.
capex_capacity: Monroe, US injectable facility received EIR with VAI classification from US FDA in November 2025; fulvestrant injection relaunched from Monroe in Q1.

Portfolio of 20-plus commercial injectables through partners; management said most are commodity products and contribution will take time, with Monroe differentiated injectables contributing from next year.
Marketing portfolio of 225 US generic products; 53 applications pending with US FDA.
Field force expansion ongoing in India and emerging markets; India MRs about 5,600, adding 300-400 per year.
Oncology commercial investments in emerging markets are built into the 21-22% margin guide; these three brands expected to yield about INR500-600 million over 5-6 years.
demand_pricing: India growth mix per management: volume about 6-7%, new products about 3%, value about 3-4%; value growth limited by high competitive intensity.
TEVIMBRA and BRUKINSA (with BeOne) exceeded INR100 crore in first 12 months; chronic respiratory GFB brand running at about INR70-80 crore annualised.
Semaglutide in India tracking at about INR20-25 crore annualised, helping turn around the diabetes franchise.
WINLEVI is a niche acne product in Europe; adoption only recently started. Branded share of Europe revenue is about 30%, targeted at about 60% over five years.
Launch of Hengrui-licensed Trastuzumab Rezetecan Phase III in platinum-resistant ovarian cancer began in India in June 2026.

qa_highlights.question: R&D spend for the quarter and incremental spend after ISB 2301 moves to clinic?
qa_highlights.answer: R&D was about INR289 crore in Q1, a bit lower than run-rate; guidance is 7-8% of revenue. IGI burn is about INR70 million, covering 2301 Phase I and trials over the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in Europe, and what share of Europe sales is branded?
qa_highlights.answer: Europe is expected to finish FY27 at high single-digit growth after four years of fastest growth; branded is about 30% of Europe revenue today, targeted at about 60% over five years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the US injectables contribution meaningful yet?
qa_highlights.answer: Not yet meaningful; most injectables are commodity products. US growth this year is driven by respiratory launches (fluticasone 44, OTC nasal spray), with Monroe differentiated injectables contributing next year.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin impact from war-related API and logistics costs, and FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Pressure is on API, packing and logistics; mitigation through product and geographic mix. Pressure may persist for at least two more quarters; full-year 21-22% margin guide retained. No quantified bps impact given.

qa_highlights.question: Will India secondary-sales convergence persist and how should India be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India can be modelled at 12-15% consistent growth; cardiovascular growing about 15%, chronic respiratory above 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital, net cash and debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital well below the 115-day full-year guide; gross debt zero maintained; operating cash of INR800-900 crore. Management declined to give a precise net cash figure.

qa_highlights.question: Status of US respiratory ANDA approvals and BioCryst ISB 830 agreement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management hopes at least two of three H2 respiratory approvals (110 mcg, nasal spray Rx, ipratropium) come through. ISB 830 backup STAR-0310 has completed Phase I; BioCryst next steps unclear after its Astria acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Status of AbbVie (ISB 2001) payments received?
qa_highlights.answer: Only the INR700 million upfront has been received, which includes the deferred income; no milestone payments received yet against the INR1.2 billion in milestones.

risks_watch: Geopolitical-driven API, packing material and freight cost inflation; management expects pressure for at least two more quarters, with margin outcome dependent on mix offsets.
Europe growth slowed to +11.9% and is guided only to high single digits in FY27; branded transition is still early.
US litigation: management says most provisions are made; two smaller litigation groups remain, with cash outflow expected within at least two years.
Concentration in India top brands (Telma and extensions); management sees no risk to growth.
Dependence on H2 FY27 US respiratory approvals (110 mcg, nasal spray Rx, ipratropium) and on Aumolertinib launch timing.
Mixing of ISB 2001 deferred income into North America growth flatters reported growth (41.1% reported vs 19.8% core).
Other income rose due to interest-rate arbitrage on working capital, while gross interest cost also rose (lease, bank commitment charges).
summary.management_tone: Confident on India, RYALTRIS and the US respiratory pipeline, but guarded on Europe growth and on cost pressure from the geopolitical situation. Management avoided giving precise net cash and cost-impact figures, deferring to balance-sheet modelling and gross-debt-zero framing.
key_quotes: We have begun FY27 on a very strong note delivering consolidated Y-o-Y revenues of 23%.
Even if you exclude the deferred income from 2001, the base business Y-o-Y growth is north of 18%.
The improved mix has also helped maintaining our gross margin in spite of the increased cost due to the ongoing geopolitical situation.
And overall, we are -- continue to maintaining our gross debt 0 position.
So as of now, we just got the INR700 million upfront. We've not got any further milestones.

adds.what: Monroe, US injectable facility (received EIR with VAI classification Nov 2025; fulvestrant relaunched from Monroe in Q1)
Field force expansion: India MRs about 5,600, adding 300-400 per year

growth.why: Q1 FY27 revenue +23.1% YoY (North America +41.1%, core +19.8%; India formulations +15.5%); management guides India 12-15% consistent growth, Europe high single digit FY27, and reiterates 21-22% EBITDA margin, backed by launches, RYALTRIS rollout and field force adds but no hard capacity numbers or order values.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management only held the 21-22% full-year margin guide and gross margin was held in Q1 despite higher API, packing and logistics costs; no expansion was guided, and cost pressure is expected to persist for at least two more quarters.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Monroe US injectable facility already has EIR/VAI and fulvestrant relaunched in Q1, with differentiated injectables expected to contribute from next year, but management says injectables are mostly commodity and not yet meaningful; field force adds 300-400 MRs per year on a base of about 5,600.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: India volume growth guided at about 6-7% within 12-15% total India growth, fluticasone 44 full-quarter benefit in Q2, RYALTRIS in 57 markets with 10 more expected, and global RYALTRIS secondary sales up more than 40% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex amount or new plant discussed; capacity utilisation not disclosed, so no basis for a new capex call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 base business grew above 18% ex-ISB 2001, India formulations +15.5% vs guided 12-15%, and two to three H2 US respiratory launches (110 mcg MDI, nasal spray Rx, ipratropium) could add upside, though management only reiterated guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management expects war-related API, packing and logistics cost pressure to persist for at least two more quarters, with no quantified bps impact, against a 21-22% full-year margin guide that was held.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two to three US respiratory launches (110 mcg MDI, nasal spray Rx, ipratropium) expected in H2 FY27, Aumolertinib India/EM launch in H2 FY27, RYALTRIS Brazil in H2 FY27, and Trastuzumab Rezetecan MA filings from Q2 FY27; QiNHAYO first launch in FY28.

rows.label: RYALTRIS rollout across more markets
rows.why: Commercialised in 57 markets with 10 more expected over coming quarters, out of more than 90 with marketing applications, and global secondary sales up upwards of 40% YoY.

rows.label: AbbVie ISB 2001 milestone payments
rows.why: Only the INR700 million upfront received so far; none of the INR1.2 billion in milestones received yet, so timing depends on trial progress in TRIgnite Phase I with more than 160 subjects dosed.

rows.label: Europe branded mix shift
rows.why: Branded share about 30% of Europe revenue, targeted at about 60% over five years; management guides high single-digit Europe growth in FY27 and double-digit from FY28 as branded launches scale.

tone.note: Management was confident on India, RYALTRIS and the US respiratory pipeline, but cautious on Europe growth and war-related cost pressure, and declined to give precise net cash or cost-impact figures; analysts pushed on the cost outlook, Europe, injectables contribution and the net cash position.
